in_text_mentions: A 67-year-old Caucasian male, who worked as a plumber, presented with a two-month history of skin fragility and pruritic blisters on dorsal hands, spreading up the arms. He noted that broken blisters healed with firm little “white spots” and described lethargy and darkening of urine. For many years he had regularly consumed three cans of beer daily. Examination revealed intact blisters alongside numerous erosions over the hands and elbows and milia on inspection of the left hand ( Figure 1). There was no forehead hypertrichosis.
